title: gpu-swarm-orchestrator-terraform-module-for-asg-karpenter-and-health-sentinels
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a reusable Terraform module that provisions GPU-backed Kubernetes node groups in Private (VPC) environments with dual autoscaling strategies (ASG + Karpenter compatibility), integrated health sentinels for instance and driver health, and a safe rolling upgrade orchestration. The module must support: heterogeneous instance types, warm standby pools for burst, GPU driver lifecycle hooks, tainting/cordon logic for evictions, and automated rollback when post-upgrade health checks fail. Target cloud: AWS (EC2/ASG + EKS + Karpenter). This ticket covers module design, initial implementation, and integration tests (unit + infra tests).
comments: 2025-02-15 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff notes. Decided to support ASG first and add Karpenter-compatible nodegroup labels so both can be targeted by the same autoscale policy. Created a Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/Private/GPU-Orchestrator-Design

2025-02-18 - Marco Chen: Implemented initial Terraform module skeleton in git: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-modules/pull/482 - exposes variables for instance_families, gpu_driver_version, warm_pool_size, and karpenter_compatibility (bool).

2025-02-21 - Riley O'Connor (SRE): Reviewed healthcheck approach. Recommended a sidecar 'sentinel-prober' DaemonSet that records driver and nvml health and exports metrics to Prometheus. Suggestion: use lifecycle hooks to block instance termination until sentinel marks node draining complete.

2025-02-24 - Marco Chen: Prototype for driver update flow uses an SSM document to update AMI bootstrapping and a GPU-driver DaemonSet for out-of-band upgrades. Trade-off: AMI bake vs runtime install. Chose a hybrid: prefer AMI with preinstalled drivers for stable fleets and fallback to DaemonSet for minor patching.

2025-02-26 - Design review: Canaries vs rolling replacement. PM (Sofia García) prefers canary pool (small heterogeneous set) to validate driver + kernel combos before full rollout. Added canary_pool_size and canary_instance_types variables.

2025-03-01 - Marco Chen: Added graceful-drain-prober hook (pre-terminate lambda) that posts to control plane to disable routing and waits for sentinel health OK before ASG terminates. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-modules/pull/497

2025-03-03 - Security review note (Tariq Rahman): Need KMS-encrypted SSM parameters for GPU driver packages and strict IAM roles for the termination hook. Marked security_review_required = true and added policy template to repo.

2025-03-03 - Marco Chen: Integration tests added to the module's terratest suite. Tests create a small EKS cluster in a sandbox VPC and validate node provisioning, sentinel metrics firing, and simulated driver failure rollback.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module publishes to internal registry with semantic versioning and README
Module can provision ASG-backed GPU node group with warm_pool and canary options in a sandbox VPC
Karpenter-compatible labels/annotations present so the same instance class can be exploited by Karpenter if enabled
Sentinel DaemonSet reports driver and NVML health to Prometheus metrics and exposes /healthz for probes
Pre-terminate lifecycle hook prevents instance termination until graceful-drain-prober confirms pods evicted or timeout
Rolling upgrade pipeline performs canary rollout to canary_pool_size then a staggered replacement; automated rollback on sentinel failures
Terratest infra tests pass end-to-end in sandbox (create -> deploy GPU workload -> upgrade drivers -> verify rollback)
